output.reason: A few days of right-hand numbness and tingling worse at night, with reported absence of weakness, facial droop or speech change, fits a common nerve-compression pattern manageable with guidance plus clear escalation triggers.
output.patientMessage: You can start with self-care: avoid bending the wrist while sleeping (a neutral wrist splint at night often helps) and ease repetitive wrist tasks. Night-worse hand tingling is commonly nerve compression at the wrist. Message a Counsel clinician if numbness becomes constant, you develop hand weakness or dropping objects, or muscle wasting appears. Call 911 for sudden face droop, slurred speech or new limb weakness.
differential: Carpal tunnel syndrome (median nerve compression at the wrist)
Other peripheral nerve compression, e.g. thoracic outlet or cervical origin

redFlags.concern: Trauma, swelling or severe pain in the arm

output.vitalSigns: No vital signs reported; whether any were measured is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Consumer health summaries describe typical carpal tunnel features but cannot confirm this patient's diagnosis without examination or nerve testing.

citations.limitation: Pattern match only; diagnosis unconfirmed without exam or nerve studies.
